title: 2003 AMC 10A Problem 23
statement: A large equilateral triangle is constructed by using toothpicks to create rows of small equilateral triangles. For example, in the figure we have \(3\) rows of small congruent equilateral triangles, with \(5\) small triangles in the base row. How many toothpicks would be needed to construct a large equilateral triangle if the base row of the triangle consists of \(2003\) small equilateral triangles?

solutions.text:
A triangle with \(n\) rows has \(2n - 1\) small triangles in its base row, so \(2n - 1 = 2003\) gives \(n = 1002.\)

Each row \(k\) requires \(3k\) toothpicks, so the total is \(3(1 + 2 + \cdots + 1002).\)

This equals \(3 \cdot \dfrac{1002 \cdot 1003}{2} = 1{,}507{,}509.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
